subject.title: cron: reject webhook URLs with embedded credentials

question: Should cron webhook URL userinfo be rejected fail-closed for existing stored jobs, or must this PR add doctor/audit migration behavior before merge?
rationale: Rejecting URL userinfo reduces secret exposure, but the shared helper also controls stored cron delivery and migration paths, so automation should not choose the security-versus-upgrade tradeoff without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require upgrade path before merge
options.body: Add doctor/audit handling, redacted warnings, focused tests, and real cron-path proof before accepting the stricter validator.

options.title: Accept fail-closed hardening
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally accept that credentialed webhook URLs stop delivering until operators edit them, but the PR should document and prove that path.

options.title: Replace with redaction-first hardening
options.body: Use a fresh current-main PR that first redacts credentialed URLs while preserving delivery compatibility until a migration policy is decided.

recommendation.title: Require upgrade path before merge
recommendation.body: Add doctor/audit handling, redacted warnings, focused tests, and real cron-path proof before accepting the stricter validator.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the cron runtime notification and doctor migration surfaces that need the policy decision.
